## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Mobile browser games

- Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
- Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
- Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
- Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

We need to build a complete playable game: "GTA 5 but with Minecraft world generation" — so an open-world sandbox crime game in a voxel blocky world, procedurally generated per seed, with cities, roads, terrain biomes, cars, pedestrians, police wanted system, shooting/driving, missions perhaps.

Approach: Build with Three.js voxel engine in browser. Need good performance. Seeded world generation: terrain biomes (plains, desert, forest, mountains, ocean), city districts with roads grid, buildings, parks, etc. The world "makes sense": cities near flat land / coast, roads connect, biome-dependent.

Gameplay requirements (GTA-like):
- Third-person character with walking, sprint, jump
- Enter/exit vehicles, driving with physics-ish arcade handling
- Pedestrians, police, wanted level
- Shooting (hitscan) with weapon
- HUD: health, wanted stars, minimap, cash
- Missions: pickups/deliveries, maybe simple "steal car and deliver" / "eliminate target" side jobs
- Seed input UI, regenerate world with same seed gives identical world
- Mobile touch controls + responsive UI (Agents.md requirement)
- Day/night maybe
- Mini-map of city roads

Need to think about scope and performance. The world should feel large. Voxel terrain: chunks generated around player. Cities generated deterministically from seed. We can build city as flat-ish grid with roads and buildings; blocks instanced meshes for performance maybe.

Design:
- Seeded PRNG (mulberry32 / xorshift) with hashed seed string -> numeric.
- Terrain: 2D value noise / simplex per seed, heightmap. Water level. Biomes from temperature/moisture noise. Height ranges. Use chunked voxel meshes — but building a full voxel world with per-block cubes is expensive. Could use Minecraft-like terrain with visible blocks only, greedy-ish face culling. Render distance ~ 6-8 chunks around player (chunk 16x16). Use merged BufferGeometry per chunk with vertex colors, face culling.

City: Choose city centers deterministically: several city sites where terrain is flat enough and above water. City radius ~ 180 units, grid roads with block size 24, roads 8 wide, sidewalks. Buildings in blocks: boxes with window patterns via canvas texture or vertex colors + emissive windows. Use InstancedMesh for buildings maybe by material/texture atlas. Buildings with varied heights (downtown taller near center). Each block may have park or parking lot.

Need world coordinate consistent with terrain. Could flatten terrain inside city (city ground at fixed elevation). Terrain height function returns city ground level in city cells. To make roads/building placement align, use city grid algorithm.

Driving: custom arcade car physics on flat ground mostly; terrain height sampling for slope. Cars drive on roads. Could keep player/cars on ground height sampled from terrain heightfield, plus buildings collision via grid occupancy query. Collision grid: block occupancy at cell resolution (e.g., 4x4 units) within city, plus building heights. Use simple AABB collision for player and car vs buildings.

Pedestrians and traffic: spawn around player, wander sidewalks; cars drive along roads (path following) — simplify traffic cars follow road network with turns. Police spawn based on wanted level, chase player.

Missions: "jobs" markers around city: car delivery, package pickup, target takedown. Money, health pickups.

Shooting: raycast hitscan onto peds/police/cars, muzzle flash, bullet tracer. Wanted level increases.

Day/night cycle with sun and sky colors; streetlights emissive at night.

Mobile: touch joystick, action buttons (jump, shoot, enter/exit), camera drag. Responsive.

Screenshots: use playwright-cli with Xvfb. Need to run local server. Use vite? Simpler: static files + npm? Browser needs modules; can use plain static server via `python3 -m http.server` or node. Use Three.js from node_modules via importmap? We can npm install three and vite for bundling. Check network availability.

We need to produce a polished game. Big task. Let's plan architecture:

Files:
- index.html
- src/main.js (bootstrap, game loop)
- src/rng.js
- src/worldgen.js (terrain noise, biomes, city layout, buildings, props)
- src/terrain.js (chunk meshes, water)
- src/city.js (roads, buildings meshes, collision)
- src/entities.js (player model, peds, cars, police)
- src/input.js (keyboard, touch, pointer lock/camera orbit)
- src/hud.js
- src/audio.js (WebAudio synth engine sounds, gunshots)
- styles.css

Maybe use no external assets; procedural geometry and canvas textures.

Key: seeded determinism. All generation from seed via PRNG streams. Cars/traffic spawns use random from seed + time? Determinism requirement is about world gen, not transient entities. Ensure world layout identical given seed.

World layout design:

Terrain:
- heightmap function h(x,z) using fractal value noise; sea level 0.
- continental shape? Use low-frequency noise for landmass.
- biomes based on second noise: forest/plains/desert/snow/mountains.
- Blocky terraces: quantize height into steps of 1.5? Minecraft feel: blocks of size 2 units. Height = floor(h / 2)*2. Terrain mesh as stepped columns with top color + side colors. We can render as voxel-ish columns: each grid cell (2x2) with top face at height and four side faces down to neighbor heights. That gives blocky Minecraft look. Use vertex colors and per-face shading; optionally texture atlas canvas to give pixel noise.

Chunk size 16 cells (32 units), render radius maybe 8 chunks = 256 units. That's fine. Terrain geometry per chunk with faces: columns 256 * visible faces. Drawing only top + exposed sides. That's efficient.

Water: transparent plane at y=0.5? Sea level. Maybe animate.

City placement:
- sample candidate city centers within some radius of origin (e.g., origin is player spawn), choose 2-3 city sites with terrain flattenable; one main city near origin within ~150 units. City ground elevation computed as median height at site, clamped above sea-level+2.
- Flatten terrain within city: blend height toward city elevation in radius; roads at city elevation.
- City layout on grid: cell size 28: road lines every 28 units; roads width 10. Blocks 18x18. City extent e.g., 9x9 blocks = 252 units. Buildings inside blocks with margin.
- Downtown: building height depends on distance to city center; heights 8-70 units. Outer: 6-16.
- Roads drawn as dark asphalt planes slightly above ground, with lane markings. Sidewalks as light gray strips.
- Buildings: boxes with window textures. Need variety: brick/concrete/glass, rooftop details. Use instanced boxes with per-instance color plus a window texture? InstancedMesh with one window texture and per-instance color tint works. Or merge geometry with vertex UVs + textures. Use 3-4 window canvas textures (glass, brick) as materials; build separate InstancedMesh per material. Rooftop boxes, AC units.

But windows need scale-appropriate UVs; per-instance UV scaling not simple. Could use a shader texture with world-space triplanar? Simpler: generate building geometry merged into one BufferGeometry with UVs that repeat based on dimensions, using a texture with wrap repeat. That means one geometry per city with maybe ~200 buildings, each ~10 faces. That's fine. Build one merged geometry with material per style. Windows are texture with rows/columns. Also emissive windows at night: use material emissiveMap same texture and emissive intensity toggled. We can make texture: dark facade with lit windows random — but fixed texture repeats visibly. Generate 8 window textures 128x128 with random window lit patterns per texture, and use different textures for few materials. At night windows glow somewhat. Could also add per-building random UV offset to vary.

Maybe use vertex colors for facade + a shader? Keep it reasonable.

We could use a single canvas texture atlas of window patterns (4x4 tiles), and each building uses different tile. That gives variety. MeshStandardMaterial with map + emissiveMap, emissive white, emissiveIntensity 0.35 at night. Texture atlas would make all windows same-ish pattern per tile but rotated/offset could vary.

Building style: make canvas texture 64x64 per style: base wall color with vertical window columns. With UV repeat set per building, pattern tiles. Textures can be generated per building style with seeded colors. Use maybe 6 materials.

Alternative simpler: use BoxGeometry per building with toon material flat colors and add window strips as separate thin emissive boxes on facades. Could be visually good and cheap: for each building, generate 2-4 window strip meshes per side? That's many meshes. Merge into geometry with emissive material; windows as quads slightly offset from facade. Vertex colors + emissive material. Night glow. Window lights random lit/unlit using vertex colors.

Better: build merged geometry with groups: facade geometry (MeshLambertMaterial vertex colors) and windows geometry (MeshBasicMaterial vertex colors, semi emissive look) with per-window colors that at night appear lit. Daytime visible dark glass. Can adjust material color based on time? MeshBasicMaterial can't be lit; windows would look flat. Maybe acceptable stylized look. Windows could be slightly reflective blue by day.

But performance: 250 buildings merged into few meshes fine.

City generation detail:
- For each block cell in grid (e.g., 9x9), decide type by seed and distance: downtown center block = plaza/park, others buildings (1-4 per block) or park/parking lot.
- Collision: register building AABBs in a spatial grid for collision queries, and add roads/blocked map.
- Pavement/sidewalk plane per block? Draw a large city ground plane with pavement color, roads on top; block interiors maybe concrete.

Road network: Need traffic path. Use grid graph of road center lines (horizontal/vertical) with intersections. Traffic cars move along lanes, choose random direction at intersections. Keep simple: cars move along road center with offset lane, at intersection pick new direction. Player can drive anywhere.

Police: chase using simple steering toward player, shoot when close. Wanted stars 0-5, decay when hidden/out of sight and time.

Gameplay loop:
- Spawn player on a sidewalk near city center.
- HUD mission prompt: go to yellow marker to start a job. Jobs: "Delivery" — steal a specific parked car and drive it to marker within time; "Hit" — eliminate target ped; "Getaway" — survive 60s at 3 stars? Keep 2-3 types generated around city.
- Cash rewards, health, armor maybe.
- Weapon: pistol with ammo infinite? Pickups: health, armor, ammo. Maybe keep pistol and SMG.

Vehicles: parked cars along roads, traffic. Enter nearest car with E. Driving: accelerate W, brake S, steer A/D, handbrake space. Camera follows behind. Speed max ~40 units/s. Collision with buildings, peds (run over -> wanted), cars. Exit with E. Radio? Maybe engine audio + horn.

On-foot: WASD mouse-look third-person (pointer lock), shift sprint, space jump, left click shoot, right click aim (zoom). Mobile: virtual joystick move, drag screen to look, buttons.

Wanted: shooting peds +2 stars, killing +? Carjack +1, hit cop +2. Stars decay.

Minimap: canvas 2D circular rotating radar showing roads/buildings, peds/cops/cars, mission marker. Compass? Nice.

World seed UI: start screen overlay with seed text + "Generate World" and random button, shows seed. Pause menu "Change seed". Same seed deterministic world. Also display seed in HUD. URL query ?seed= for sharing? Good: sync seed to URL hash (not necessary but nice). If hash present, auto-start.

Note: user asked "You choose the world seed so you're able to get the same world over again using the same seed." So allow entering seed. Show seed prominently, copy button maybe.

Also "GTA 5 but with Minecraft world generation" — could mean the GTA map generated Minecraft-style: blocky terrain, cities. Ensure Minecraft aesthetic: blocky trees, voxel terrain, blocky characters/cars (angular low-poly), block breaking? GTA doesn't need mining. Maybe allow destroying environment? Could add melee/shooting breaks windows? Keep focus: driving + shooting + world.

Could add "blocky destruction": shooting cars causes explosions; destructible props (barrels, streetlights). Nice.

Day/night: 8-minute cycle; shadows? Directional light with shadows could be expensive; use one shadow map 2048 limited area near player. Maybe disable shadows on mobile; use blob shadows under characters/cars? For style, use directional shadow following player, buildings cast shadows. Shadow camera ~120 units. Terrain receive? Terrain chunks receiveShadow. City buildings cast. Performance may be okay with SwiftShader? Headless screenshots at SwiftShader could be slow. Need a decent capture. Maybe shadows off by default with simple ambient occlusion? Could still be fine but capture needs fast. Use baked-ish look: vertex shading on terrain, directional light. Let's try shadow map 1024, only city area; check performance in browser. Given SwiftShader CPU, the game may run 10-20fps at 1280x720 — screenshot okay.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable browser game: “GTA 5 but with Minecraft world generation”, with seeded procedural worlds that regenerate identically from the same seed.

## Requirements
- Each world must be different but coherent (terrain, city, roads).
- User chooses/enters the world seed; same seed reproduces the same world.
- Build the full playable game now; do not ask clarifying questions, make reasonable assumptions.
- Save small JPEG screenshots for self-checks (viewport ≤1280px wide); read only latest; full-size PNG only for fine detail.
- Mobile/touch support per repo guidance (responsive, safe areas, touch controls).

## Decisions
- Browser Three.js + Vite game titled **GRAND THEFT BLOCK — San Voxel**.
- Voxel/blocky Minecraft aesthetic: stepped terrain, blocky trees/buildings/characters/cars.
- Seeded generation from hashed seed strings; all layout deterministic via `stream(seed, name)`.
- City is always the spawn area on a flattened plateau; terrain uses layered value/ridge noise outside it (plains, forest, desert, snow, rock, beach, ocean).
- Procedural city: 9×9 lots, road grid, sidewalks, skyscrapers with tiered facades and lit-window emissive maps, parks, parking lots, plaza/fountain, construction sites, streetlights, palms, crosswalks.
- GTA-style gameplay: on-foot movement/swimming, pistol, third-person camera, enter/carjack any car, arcade driving, traffic AI, pedestrians, police/wanted stars, health/armor/cash, jobs (delivery, hit, checkpoint race), day/night, minimap, world map, notifications, death/respawn, synthesised WebAudio.
- World seed shown in HUD/start screen; seed also stored in URL hash.

## Work State
### Completed
- Project scaffold: `package.json` (three ^0.187.0, vite ^7.1.0), `index.html`, `src/style.css` (full HUD/start/pause/map/mobile UI).
- Core utilities: `src/rng.js` (hashString, mulberry32, named streams, value noise, fbm, ridge, randomSeed, formatSeed), `src/textures.js` (terrain noise, facade + emissive maps, glow/star/water textures).
- World generation modules:
  - `src/world/height.js` — constants, biome colours, natural/quantised heights, city flattening, biome/slope/water queries.
  - `src/world/geo.js` — `GeoBuilder` (quad/tri/box/flat/cylinder), colour helpers.
  - `src/world/city.js` — city layout, building tiers, colliders, parking spots, walk/job points, all city meshes, street props, map-building metadata.
  - `src/world/chunks.js` — chunked voxel terrain meshes, biomes, trees/cacti/pines/rocks, chunk streaming.
  - `src/world/sky.js` — sky shader, sun/moon/stars/clouds, water, day-night lighting, window/streetlight emissive, fog.
  - `src/world/index.js` — `World` orchestration, collision grid/resolution, static raycasts, map canvas, location/biome labels, dispose.
- Gameplay modules: `src/characters.js`, `src/input.js`, `src/audio.js`, `src/particles.js`, `src/vehicles.js`, `src/player.js`, `src/peds.js`, `src/items.js`, `src/missions.js`, `src/hud.js`.
- Main UI additions: `#damage-flash` in `index.html`, cash-pop/damage-flash CSS.

### Active
- `src/game.js` (Game class) is **not yet written** — must tie together world, player, vehicles, peds, items, missions, HUD, camera, input, audio, start screen, pause/map/death, wanted/police, shooting, prompts, seed rebuild flow.
- `src/main.js` is **not yet written** — boot renderer/resize/animation loop.
- Dependencies not installed yet; no build/test/screenshot has been run.
- Known integration TODOs:
  - Add `VehicleManager.raycast(origin, dir, maxDist)` for shooting cars.
  - Call `game.missions?.onVehicleDestroyed(this)` from `Vehicle.explode`; `Vehicle.explode` currently calls missing `game.exitVehicle(true)`.
  - `Game` must provide `spawnCashPickup`, `spawnCopFromCar`, `notify`, `registerCrime`, `killPlayer`, `exitVehicle`, `onDistrictChange`, `hud`, `cameraZoomDelta`, `cameraShake`, seed/time/state.
  - Remove/ignore `missions.updateAvailablePrompt()` prompt side effects; Game should centralise prompts.
  - Mission starts should set `job.status='active'` (already patched) and clear job marker visibility.
  - `PedManager.spawnTarget` added; mission code uses it.
  - `VehicleManager.populate` uses hero parked cars near plaza; verify no overlaps.
  - `src/world/geo.js` cylinder top uses `addTri` fix (done).
  - `src/world/chunks.js` neighbour grid indexing fixed to 18×18 border grid.
  - Check `src/world/index.js` imports unused `hashString`, `STEP`; harmless.
  - `Environment.update` creates `new THREE.Color` per frame in several places (minor perf).
  - `Player` imports `wrapAngle` from `vehicles.js`; verify no circular init issue.
  - `body.mobile` class must be set by Game/boot for mobile CSS.
  - `#start-screen` must be initial visible; `#hud` hidden initially; `#loading` hidden initially.
  - `#rotate-hint` exists but should likely remain hidden.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Write `src/game.js`: renderer/scene/camera setup, `buildSession(seed)`, menu preview orbit, `enterGame`, `quitToMenu`, `disposeSession`, `startGame` seed compare/rebuild, start-screen button bindings, seed UI, auto-start `?play=1`, URL hash seed.
2. Implement gameplay loop states (`menu`, `playing`, `paused`, `map`, `dead`), input consume, player/vehicle/ped/item/mission updates, camera update, shooting (peds/vehicles/static), interactions (E enter/exit/job), prompts, wanted/police spawning/decay, death/respawn, audio engine/siren, HUD/minimap update.
3. Add `VehicleManager.raycast`; wire `missions.onVehicleDestroyed`, `onVehicleEntered`, `onPedKilled`; implement `spawnCashPickup`, `spawnCopFromCar`, `registerCrime`, `killPlayer`, `exitVehicle`.
4. Write `src/main.js` boot (renderer, resize, animation loop, loading/start flow, expose `window.__game`, readiness flag).
5. `npm install`, `npm run build`, run static server via `start.sh` with `RUNTIME_DIR=/home/runner/work/_temp/omgithub-runtime PORT=3002` in a persistent tmux session.
6. Open with `playwright-cli`, check console errors, screenshot start screen and gameplay at ≤1280px JPEG paths; verify driving, entering cars, missions, police, minimap, mobile layout, seed determinism.
7. Fix visual/perf bugs, then commit changes.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/game.js`: missing central Game orchestrator.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/main.js`: missing boot entry.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html`: DOM IDs/UI structure all modules depend on.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/style.css`: HUD/start/pause/map/mobile styling.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/world/index.js`: World API, collision, raycast, map.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/world/city.js`: city data, colliders, job/parked/walk points.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/vehicles.js`: Vehicle/VehicleManager; needs raycast + explode hook.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/player.js`: movement, camera rig, weapon state.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/peds.js`: Ped/PedManager, shooting target raycast.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/missions.js`: job state machine/markers.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/hud.js`: DOM updates, minimap, big map.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/input.js`: keyboard/mouse/touch input.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/audio.js`: synthesized audio singleton.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/particles.js`: effects/tracers.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/items.js`: pickups.

## Important Context
- Working dir: `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround`; git repo; only initial commit `4e9bdba`.
- Node v22.23.4, npm 10.9.9; 4 CPUs, ~15 GB RAM.
- `start.sh` runs `${RUNTIME_DIR}/scripts/default-start.mjs`; `RUNTIME_DIR` is `/home/runner/work/_temp/omgithub-runtime`; supports Vite build/serve, defaults port 3000 (`PORT=3002` recommended per repo guidance).
- `playwright-cli` available with headed Chromium/Xvfb/SwiftShader config at `~/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json`; use `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002`, then screenshot.
- Target screenshots: JPEG, viewport ≤1280 px wide; inspect latest only.
- World seed API: `formatSeed()` normalises; `stream(seed,label)` deterministic; URL should support `#seed=...` and `?play=1`.
- Current `Game` integration assumptions:
  - Player has `mode: 'foot'|'vehicle'`, `vehicle`, `cameraYaw/pitch`, `hp/armor/cash/wanted/ammo/reserve`.
  - Vehicle has `driver: 'player'|'ai'|null`, `police`, `pos`, `yaw`, `speed`, `enter()/exit()`, `damage()`, `explode()`.
  - `MissionSystem` exposes `jobs`, `active`, `update(dt)`, `canInteract()`, `interact(job)`, `onVehicleEntered(v)`, `onPedKilled(ped)`, `onVehicleDestroyed(v)`, `getMissionInfo()`, `fail(reason)`.
  - HUD exposes `update(dt)`, `setPrompt(html)`, `notify(...)`, `showBanner`, `damageFlash`, `popCash`, `setInVehicle`, `showDeath`, `setPauseStats`, `showMap`, `drawBigMap`.
  - Environment: `getClock()`, `getDayLabel()`, `setShadows()`, `update()`, `nightFactor`.
  - `VehicleManager`: `list`, `populate()`, `update(dt)`, `nearest(pos,maxDist)`, `spawn(opts)`, `remove(v)`, `spawnPoliceCar(pos,rng)`.
- No screenshots or build verification has been performed yet.
